        - heading "Understand Phase Plane" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A phase plane plots two state variables against each other. A useful rule is System form: dx/dt=f(x,y), dy/dt=g(x,y). You can learn Phase Plane by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: "Use System form: dx/dt=f(x,y), dy/dt=g(x,y). Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison."
        - paragraph: "In real life, predator-prey: Two populations form state points. Watch out: Reading the phase plane as time on the horizontal axis. Axes are state variables; time is traced along curves."

      - article:
        - heading "What's happening?" [level=2]
        - paragraph: This system is a center. Trajectories are closed orbits (circles) around the origin. The motion is periodic and the amplitude (radius) is constant.
      - article:
        - heading "Common misconception" [level=2]:
          - text: Common misconception
        - paragraph:
          - text: Thinking trajectories spiral in or out.
          - text: Not here—neither x nor y grows or decays. Energy (r² = x² + y²) stays constant.
      - heading "Governing system" [level=2]
      - strong:
        - text: dx/dt = y
        - text: dy/dt = −x
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Interpretation:"
        - text: • x increases when y > 0 and decreases when y < 0.
        - text: • y decreases when x > 0 and increases when x < 0.
        - text: • The origin (0, 0) is a center (stable).
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Equilibrium:"
        - text: Set dx/dt = 0, dy/dt = 0 ⇒ x = 0, y = 0.
      - heading "Worked example" [level=2]
      - paragraph:
        - text: Use x₀ = 1, y₀ = 0.
        - text: "Solution:"
        - text: x(t) = x₀ cos t + y₀ sin t = cos t
        - text: y(t) = −x₀ sin t + y₀ cos t = −sin t
        - text: "Orbit: x² + y² = 1"
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Check at t = π/2:"
        - text: x(π/2) = 0
        - text: y(π/2) = −1
        - text: "Point on plot:"
        - emphasis: (0, −1)
      - paragraph:
        - text: Self-check
        - text: "Verify: x²(t) + y²(t) = 1"
        - text: cos²t + sin²t = 1 ✓
        - text: Constant radius confirmed.
      - article:
        - heading "Quick practice" [level=2]
        - paragraph: 1. For the system dx/dt = y, dy/dt = −x, classify the equilibrium at (0, 0).
        - button "Stable node"

      - article:
